subject: Endgame: acceptance runway, exit gates, and proofpoints for Mediforge evaluation
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@mediforge.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft acceptance runway + success criteria (MAP) for Mediforge evaluation

Hi Daniel —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Attached is a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that lays out the evaluation runway, the objective success criteria we discussed, and proposed acceptance tests so both teams can validate the pilot. High-level summary below and a few asks at the end.

Quick summary (TL;DR)
- Evaluation window: 4 weeks pilot (pilot week 1 = integration & smoke; weeks 2–3 = workload validation; week 4 = performance/observability & acceptance)
- Primary success metrics: 95th percentile latency < 450ms for 1–2k QPS synthetic fan-out (chat inference), accuracy/concordance baseline >= 92% on our shared test set, and no PII leakage incidents in scanning tranche.
- Exit gates (must pass all to sign):
  1) Integration: successful VPC peering + KMS key exchange and sample inference end-to-end with your staging dataset.
  2) Performance: sustained 95th < 450ms under target concurrency with no more than 3 SLO infra alerts.
  3) Quality: model responses meeting concordance threshold on random 500-case sample.
  4) Security & compliance: SOC2 evidence items submitted (we attached the minimal checklist).

Acceptance tests (examples)
- Smoke: run our quick-check script to validate auth, model selection, and streaming.
- Load: 30-minute soak at target QPS with trace sampling; compare token cost and latency.
- Regression: run the 500-case concordance runner; produce diff report.
- Safety scan: run redaction/PII scanner on 1k outputs; verify zero high-risk exposures.

Attachments included: Mediforge_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP, timeline, owners), Mediforge_Security_QA.pdf (SOC2 item checklist).

Asks
1) Can you confirm procurement timeframe and which legal point-person should receive the draft SOW?
2) Are the evaluation metrics above aligned with internal success definitions (especially latency threshold)?
3) If yes to both, we’ll lock dates: integration week starting Aug 24 and pilot beginning Aug 31.

If anything looks off, flag it and we’ll iterate fast.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0173

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@mediforge.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@mediforge.com, ops@mediforge.com
Date: Thu, 06 Aug 2026 10:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Draft acceptance runway + success criteria (MAP) for Mediforge evaluation

Jasmine —

Appreciate the clear plan and the MAP doc. A few quick notes from our side after a light review:
- Latency threshold: 450ms 95th is reasonable if it’s measured end-to-end from our gateway. Can you confirm the exact measurement point?
- Procurement: procurement@mediforge.com is looped; our legal lead (Simran Kaur) will own SOW redlines. Expect ~5–7 business days to review a clean SOW.
- Security: the SOC2 checklist is good; ops asked for an abbreviated evidence list for network configs (VPC flow logs + KMS audit path).

We have one request: can you add an explicit canary rollback criterion in the MAP? If the pilot shows a >5% drop in intent classification on our key customer segment during the first 48 hours, we need an automatic fallback.

I attached a short internal scoping note from ops that lists the FQDNs and IP ranges we’ll use.

Thanks — I’ll confirm procurement timelines once Simran weighs in.

—Daniel
Director of Platform Engineering | Mediforge
daniel.park@mediforge.com

Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft acceptance runway + success criteria (MAP) for Mediforge evaluation

Jasmine / Laura —

Looping back after reading Daniel’s asks. Proposed edits to the MAP:
1) Measurement point: we’ll instrument RTT at the API gateway (post-auth, pre-stream merge) and include a short appendix with curl-based measurement steps so Mediforge can replicate.
2) Canary rollback: add rule — if concordance drops >5% OR error-rate >1% in rolling 1-hour window during canary (first 24–48h), auto-switch to baseline model and notify both teams + CS.
3) Evidence list: create a minimal evidence packet for procurement (VPC flow logs snippet, KMS audit sample, service account access matrix).

I drafted a short paragraph to paste into the SOW clarifying acceptance is contingent on passing all four exit gates within the pilot window or an agreed remediation plan with mutually defined remediation SLAs.

We should also propose a small extension clause: if the performance gate fails narrowly (+/- 5% on latency), allow a single 1-week extension for tuning (with a cap on additional cost). Thoughts?

—Aditya
Head of Solutions Architecture | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, procurement@mediforge.com
Date: Tue, 12 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft acceptance runway + success criteria (MAP) for Mediforge evaluation — confirmed next steps

Daniel —

Thanks for the quick feedback and for surfacing the procurement owner. We incorporated the changes Aditya suggested and updated the MAP and SOW draft. Key updates (attached SOW-Mediforge-draft.docx / updated MAP tab):
- Measurement: 95th percentile latency measured at the Mediforge API gateway (we include the curl-based script in the appendix).
- Canary rollback: explicit rollback trigger added (concordance >5% degradation OR error-rate >1% in 60m rolling window) with automatic switchover to baseline model and immediate incident bridge.
- Evidence packet: condensed VPC/KMS/flow-logs checklist for procurement.
- Extension clause: one-time 7-day tuning window if performance misses by <=5%; Redwood to discount tuning run costs by 50% for that week.

Proposed timeline (finalized):
- Integration week (owners: Mediforge ops + Redwood infra): Aug 24–28
- Pilot (validation): Aug 31–Sep 25 (4 weeks, per MAP)
- Decision review & sign: Sep 28–30 (internal sign-off meetings)

Next asks from our side:
1) Procurement: please confirm Simran Kaur’s email or the right legal alias so we can push the SOW to DocuSign.
2) Ops: confirm the FQDN/IP ranges in mediforge_ops_scope.txt — if green, we’ll schedule the integration call for Aug 24.

We’ll also create an acceptance runbook (checklist + owners + run commands) and drop it in the HubSpot record HS-93452 by EOD Aug 13.

If this looks good I’ll publish the MAP as v2 and start the SOW routing.

Thanks,
Jasmine
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com
